candidates.structural_interaction: Reach amplifying reach — developmental instinct without definition or counterforce
candidates.k2_overview: Your Wood moves as the Twin: growth that stands beside others without leaning on them. You rise the way two trees share a hillside, close enough to shelter each other, rooted enough to stand alone. Ambition, for you, is upward and personal. You measure yourself against your own last season, and quietly against the tree beside you.
candidates.k2_functional: Your stamina is vegetal: quiet, continuous, renewed by daylight and outdoor air.

k2_domain_readings.Peers: Your peers are the grove: people growing the same direction at their own speeds. Comparison is your fertilizer and your poison, so use the grove for shade and shelter, and race only your own rings.
k2_domain_readings.Independence: Wood independence is having your own soil: your plot, your craft, your income no one else waters. Secure it early. You bend badly when planted in someone else’s garden.
k2_domain_readings.Self-reliance: You hold yourself up through storms that flatten louder people, and you rarely mention the wind afterward. Let someone stake you when you are newly transplanted. It is not dependence. It is horticulture.

angles.drive: Doing it alone comes before any plan you make. Owing nobody feels safer to you, so you do the whole thing yourself sooner than hand off a piece. What you build is yours from the first nail to the last.
angles.cost_self: Whenever help comes near, you do the thing alone first. Being helped feels like debt, so you would rather do it tired than owe. Your hardest weeks are carried on one pair of shoulders.
angles.cost_others: Your own two hands are the only ones you count on. Doing it alone matters more than being carried, and that keeps your friends outside every hard week. People who would gladly help seldom get the chance to be needed by you.

angles.drive: Fast or slow around you, you move at your own speed. Being your own clock keeps you steady, since a borrowed pace never feels like yours. Nobody rushes you into a decision you would regret.
angles.cost_self: Where a sprint would get you in, you keep your pace instead. You would sooner be late on your terms than rushed on another's, since borrowed tempo is never yours. Some doors shut while you are still walking towards them.
angles.cost_others: Your pace is one thing you never change for company. Keeping your own speed matters more than keeping step, and that leaves your people waiting or going ahead. Days out with you often split into two groups.

angles.drive: You are the same person in any company. Holding one standard for yourself keeps your footing, since a new shape for each group would cost you your measure. Friends never have to guess which you will turn up.
angles.cost_self: Whenever the moment calls for a softer you, you show up as usual. You would rather stay the same than be liked for a performance, since an adjusted self is hard to trust. Some tenderness passes you by.
angles.cost_others: Holding yourself to one standard means holding friends to it. Staying the same matters more than meeting anyone halfway, and an off day gets no slack. In a hard week, the people close to you get no softer version of you.

angles.drive: Asking comes last, well after the point where it would have worked. You hold more of yourself than one load needs, and you carry all of it instead of owing anyone a piece. You are allowed to owe someone a piece of the load.
angles.cost_self: Your hands are all you trust with hard jobs. Asking feels like admitting a shortfall, and you take the long way alone ahead of the short way with help. You pay for asking no one in rest you skip, and the bill is only yours.
angles.cost_others: Whenever an offer comes, you have already finished alone. Owing nothing counts for more than being close, and that keeps your nearest people outside every struggle. By asking no one, you leave them no way to be needed by you.

angles.drive: You walk into most arguments already sure. More of you shows up than the argument needs, and the extra feels like proof, so you hold your view ahead of hearing theirs. You lose, by being right every time, the chance to be told something new.
angles.cost_self: Being right is a comfort you never run out of. Admitting a mistake feels like losing part of yourself, and you defend a wrong call as much as a right one. You come out of each argument right and without the lesson it held.
angles.cost_others: Where you are sure, you leave no space for anyone partly right. Holding your view matters more than hearing theirs, and that costs people near you their say. Each time you win the point, you cost them the pleasure of changing your mind.

angles.drive: A little distance is your default with almost everyone. There is more of you than you want anyone handling, and you keep people at arm's length instead of letting them close. You keep that distance for safety, and it keeps the company out as well.
angles.cost_self: Keeping your distance is the habit that costs most and shows least. You would rather be a little alone than fully known, and you stay just out of reach. Out of reach, you miss the very closeness you keep out.
angles.cost_others: You hold people at a distance that feels polite from your side. Being left alone matters more than being reached for, and that gives your friends no way in. With that distance, you cost them a friend they could have reached.

edge.lead: Wood runs through your family, your growth and your social life. It is the calm of standing on your own at home, the pace you keep while the street rushes past, and the friend whose voice stays the same in every crowd.
